title: Activation Cadence Timerboard and Contingency Tasks
body:
Purpose:
This is a compact, operational-first checklist + timerboard for activation cadence: what to watch, when to act, and exactly who flips which switches during a customer-facing rollout. Focused on minimizing latency surprises, maintaining cost targets, and ensuring graceful fallbacks. Audience: product ops, SRE, console, customer success, release leads.

TL;DR:
- Staggered ramp over 48 hours, with four hard gates (0h, +3h, +12h, +48h).
- Primary KPIs: P50 latency, error-rate (5xx), token cost per request, successful session ratio.
- If any gate crosses trigger thresholds, enact immediate throttle + notify execs + roll back to canary model.

Activation cadence (timerboard): relative times are from first traffic redirect (T0). Owners listed as initials.
- T-21d: Finalize rollout config, capacity budget, and traffic plan. Owner: SR. Artifacts: feature-flag YAML, capacity ticket.
- T-7d: Dry-run traffic (internal) at 30% of expected QPS for 2 hours. Owner: JM. Confirm telemetry ingestion.
- T-2d: Observability smoke: dashboards, alerts, run synthetic prompt set. Owner: MS.
- T-0 (first redirect, 0h): Route 5% traffic. Monitor first 30 minutes closely. Owner: RL.
- T+3h: Auto-scale target increase to support 25% planned throughput. Gate check at +3h. Owner: EM.
- T+12h: Evaluate quality metrics (sampling of 500 sessions), adjust model variant if drift > 3%. Owner: Product-ML.
- T+24h: Increase to 60% if KPIs green. Prepare for full ramp at +48h. Owner: SR.
- T+48h: Full traffic roll (100%) if all gates green and long-tail latency within target. Owner: Release Lead.
- T+72h: Post-launch retrospective notes and carry-forward tickets. Owner: Product Ops.

KPI tracker (single-line entries for quick copy/paste into dashboards):
- P50 latency: target <= 120ms for inference-only calls; source = telemetry-inference.adapters; owner = SRE.
- P95 latency: target <= 420ms; if P95 > 600ms at any gate -> roll back to previous model variant.
- Error rate (5xx): target <= 0.5%; if >1.0% sustained for 5m -> throttle to 30%.
- Token cost per request: target <= $0.015 (avg); owner = FinOps / Product Ops.
- Successful session ratio: target >= 98%; if <95% -> trigger quality hold and rollback to canary.
- KV cache hit rate: target >= 72% within first 12h; if <50% investigate routing and cache warmup.
- Model quality regression (eval set): delta <= 0.7% absolute; if >0.7% -> hold rollout and call ML on-call.

Launch hour runbook (concise actionable steps):
- 00:00 (redirect): Flip FF: product-launch-2025-activation -> 5% traffic. Channel: #launch-ops. Owner: SR.
- 00:05: Confirm Telemetry: dashboards up, right data streams. Owner: JM. Checklist: request logs, latency histograms, token counters.
- 00:15: Sampling: capture 50 random sessions for manual QA. Owner: CS lead.
- 00:30: Gate check: if all green, increase to 15%. Owner: RL. If any trigger, run immediate throttle sequence (see contingency).
- +3h: Manual COA (change of action) sync: 15-minute stand to decide + next ramp. Owner: Release Lead.

Contingency playbook (triggers and exact responses):
- Trigger A — P95 > 900ms for 2 minutes: Action: immediately reduce traffic by 50% (FF -> 50% of current), call infra-oncall, enable aggressive batching offload policy. Escalation: page SRE.
- Trigger B — 5xx > 1% for 5 continuous minutes: Action: throttle writes/long-running endpoints to 10 TPS, roll traffic back to canary model variant, create incident H1.
- Trigger C — sudden cost spike (token-cost/request > 2x baseline for 15m): Action: switch to cheaper quantized variant for new sessions, pause non-critical background batch jobs, notify finance lead.
- Trigger D — model quality regression (eval delta > 1%): Action: immediately stop ramp, enable fallback to model-v2-canary, open priority ML investigation ticket.

Feature flags and run-time knobs (exact keys):
- product_launch.activation_percent (0-100) -> primary traffic steering knob.
- product_launch.model_variant -> values: stable | canary | quantized-cheap | experimental.
- infra_throttle.global_qps_limit -> numeric cap applied by SRE.
- telemetry.sample_rate_override -> used to ramp up sampling on early traffic.

Communication templates (short):
- Incident slack post (50 chars summary): "Launch: P95 spike -> throttled to 50%, investigating (see incident link)."
- Exec summary email (subject): "Launch Day Hour X: Status, Next Steps, Risks". Body bullet: one-line KPI statuses, one-line action, ETA for next check.

Dependencies and pre-reqs (blocking tickets to clear):
- capacity-provisioning: CLOUD-1422 (GPU pool resize), owner: Infra Eng.
- feature-flag rollout review: PR-87 (GH), owner: DevEx.
- telemetry mapping: OBS-501 (dashboard wiring), owner: Observability.

Open questions / To-do (notes-to-self style):
- Q1: Is synthetic prompt set reflective of real user behavior during peak? (Action: ask Product Research by T-7d).
- Q2: Do we have permission to switch to quantized variant for regulated customers? (Action: legal check).
- TODO: Add a short canned customer message for CS in case of quality hold.
- TODO: Confirm cost accounting tag propagation for token cost attribution across infra.

Post-launch (24-72h) checklist:
- 24h: Confirm long-tail latency & error trends stable. Owner: SRE.
- 48h: Final traffic shift if all gates stayed green. Owner: Release Lead.
- 72h: Run a cross-team retrospective; produce a one-page incident-free summary and action items. Owner: Product Ops.

Quick reference (who to page):
- SRE on-call: pagerduty:SRE-main
- ML on-call: pagerduty:ml-inference
- Release lead: Slack @robin-lee
- CS escalation: Slack @maya-singh

Notes: keep this doc lean. The intent is to be copy-pastable into the launch channel at T-0. If something in the timerboard changes, increment the doc version (bottom) and ping the stakeholders list.

Version history:
- v0.1 2025-02-12 draft initial timerboard (SR).
- v0.2 2025-02-15 incorporated SRE feedback on triggers (JM).
- v0.3 2025-02-18 added cost knobs and updated owners (SR, MS).
